generatedNote: Gaply's OWN manuscript scaffolds, informed by publishers' PUBLIC author guidance. NOT copied templates, NOT official. Section keys are shared across scaffolds so switching preserves matching content.
globalNotice: These are Gaply's own structures to help you start — not official publisher templates. Always check the venue's current author guidelines (linked). Gaply formats structure + references; the publisher typesets the final layout. Free to use.

scaffolds.label: Generic IMRaD (journal)
scaffolds.noticeText: A general IMRaD structure (Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion) — Gaply's own starting scaffold, not tied to any publisher. Follow your target journal's guidelines.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: One paragraph: problem, method, key result, significance. Usually no citations.

sections.heading: Keywords
sections.guidance: 3–6 comma-separated indexing terms.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Motivate the problem, state the gap and your contribution.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.guidance: Enough detail to reproduce: data, materials, procedures, analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.guidance: What you found, without interpretation. Figures and tables here.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Interpret results against the gap; limitations; implications.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.guidance: Restate the contribution and future work. Keep it short.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: Gaply will insert your library citations in the chosen style (Set B). For now, list manually if needed.

docxFormat.source: Gaply academic default following common IMRaD/ICMJE review-manuscript practice (double-spaced, continuous line numbers, 12pt serif, 1-inch margins). No single publisher owns this format.

latexFormat.source: Single-column, the same shape as the .docx manuscript export. No publisher owns the IMRaD structure, so there is no journal look to read it in.

scaffolds.label: IEEE-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: IEEE-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by IEEE's public author guidance — not an official IEEE template. Verify current requirements (and pick your exact template) at the IEEE Author Center; a template selector is also linked in the guidance.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: Self-contained, no citations, ~150–250 words. IEEE abstracts state purpose, method, results, conclusions.

sections.heading: Index Terms
sections.guidance: IEEE calls keywords 'Index Terms' — alphabetical, from the IEEE taxonomy where possible.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Problem, motivation, and contributions as an explicit list.

sections.heading: Related Work
sections.guidance: Position against prior work; make the delta explicit.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.guidance: System/approach in enough detail to reproduce.

sections.heading: Experiments and Results
sections.guidance: Setup, baselines, metrics, and results (tables/figures).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Interpretation, threats to validity, limitations.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.guidance: Contribution recap + future work.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: IEEE numeric style [1], in citation order. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Section numbering follows IEEE's Roman-numeral convention (I., II., …). Spacing/font/margins are Gaply review-manuscript defaults. IEEE's OFFICIAL article format is a two-column camera-ready template typeset by IEEE — NOT reproduced here (single-column manuscript only).

latexFormat.source: Two-column with Roman section numerals, which is how IEEE's published articles read. Produced with the generic article class, NOT IEEEtran — a reading layout, not an IEEE submission.

scaffolds.label: ACM-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: ACM-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by ACM's public submission guidance — not an official ACM template (acmart). Verify current requirements at the ACM author page.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: Concise, self-contained; ~150–250 words.

sections.heading: CCS Concepts
sections.guidance: ACM Computing Classification System concepts (generated via the ACM CCS tool).

sections.heading: Keywords
sections.guidance: Author keywords beyond the CCS concepts.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Problem, motivation, and contributions.

sections.heading: Related Work
sections.guidance: Prior work and your distinction from it.

sections.heading: Method
sections.guidance: Approach/system design.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.guidance: Study/experiment design, metrics, and findings.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Interpretation and limitations.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.guidance: Recap and future work.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: ACM reference format. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Line numbers + single-column reflect ACM's 'manuscript/review' submission mode; decimal section numbering per ACM. Spacing/font/margins are Gaply defaults. ACM's camera-ready acmart layout is typeset by ACM — not reproduced.

latexFormat.source: Two-column, decimal sections, as ACM's published articles read. Produced with the generic article class, NOT acmart.

scaffolds.label: Springer LNCS-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: LNCS-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by Springer's public LNCS author guidance — not the official Springer LNCS template. Verify current requirements at the Springer LNCS author page (LaTeX support also linked in the guidance).

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: LNCS abstracts are short — roughly 70–150 words, no references.

sections.heading: Keywords
sections.guidance: LNCS requires keywords, separated by middle dots.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Context, problem, and contribution.

sections.heading: Related Work
sections.guidance: Prior work and positioning.

sections.heading: Method
sections.guidance: Approach and formal/technical detail.

sections.heading: Results and Evaluation
sections.guidance: Experiments, proofs, or evaluation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.guidance: Summary and outlook.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: LNCS reference style. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Decimal numbered sections + A4 per Springer LNCS convention. Spacing (1.5) / font / margins are Gaply review-manuscript defaults. LNCS's final 10pt template is typeset by Springer — not reproduced.

latexFormat.source: Springer LNCS papers are published single-column on A4; that is the reading layout. Produced with the generic article class, NOT llncs.

scaffolds.label: Elsevier-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: Elsevier-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by Elsevier's public author guidance — not an official Elsevier template. Reference styles vary by journal; verify at the Elsevier author page (LaTeX instructions also linked).

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: Single paragraph (or structured if the journal requires); state purpose, methods, results, conclusions.

sections.heading: Keywords
sections.guidance: Up to ~6 keywords for indexing.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Background and objectives; avoid a detailed literature survey.

sections.heading: Materials and Methods
sections.guidance: Sufficient detail to reproduce; cite established methods.

sections.heading: Results
sections.guidance: Clear and concise findings.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Significance without repeating results; a combined Results and Discussion is sometimes allowed.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.guidance: Main conclusions, possibly as a short standalone section.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: Journal-specific (often Elsevier Vancouver or Harvard). Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Elsevier commonly asks for double-spaced manuscripts with continuous line numbering and decimal numbered sections (1., 2., 2.1) for review. Font/margins/page size are Gaply defaults; exact rules are journal-specific — verify at the link.

latexFormat.source: Two-column A4, as most Elsevier journals publish. Produced with the generic article class, NOT elsarticle.

scaffolds.label: Nature-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: Nature-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by Nature's public formatting guide — not an official Nature template. Note Nature places Methods after the main text; verify current requirements at the Nature author page.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: Unstructured summary, ~150–200 words, no references, accessible to a broad audience.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Nature main text opens without a heading; keep the context tight and broad.

sections.heading: Results
sections.guidance: Findings with figures; subheadings allowed.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Interpretation and significance; Nature keeps this concise.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.guidance: Nature places Methods AFTER the main text — reproducible detail, online.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: Nature numbered style, limited count for Letters. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Nature's formatting guide specifies double-spaced manuscripts with continuous line numbering and unnumbered sections (Methods placed after the main text). Font/margins/page size are Gaply defaults (Nature does not mandate a submission font).

latexFormat.source: Two-column with unnumbered sections, as Nature publishes. Nature has no official public LaTeX class; this is Gaply's reading approximation.

scaffolds.label: PLOS-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: PLOS-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by PLOS's public formatting guidelines — not an official PLOS template. Verify current requirements at the PLOS author page.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: ≤300 words, no citations; structured for clinical trials.

sections.heading: Author Summary
sections.guidance: Optional non-technical summary (some PLOS journals), ~150–200 words.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Background and rationale for a broad readership.

sections.heading: Materials and Methods
sections.guidance: Full detail for reproducibility; ethics statements as required.

sections.heading: Results
sections.guidance: Findings with figures/tables.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Interpretation, limitations, and implications; PLOS may combine with a short Conclusions.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: PLOS numbered (Vancouver-like) style. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Grounded in PLOS submission guidelines (fetched): 'Manuscript text should be double-spaced'; 'Use continuous line numbers'; abstract not exceeding 300 words, no citations. PLOS allows 'any standard font' — so 12pt Times New Roman, 1-inch margins, and Letter are Gaply defaults.

latexFormat.source: PLOS publishes single-column; line numbers are kept because PLOS asks for them in review. Gaply's reading layout, not a PLOS template.

scaffolds.label: MDPI-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: MDPI-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by MDPI's public author guidance — not an official MDPI template. Verify current requirements at the MDPI author page.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: Single paragraph, ~200 words: background, methods, results, conclusion.

sections.heading: Keywords
sections.guidance: 3–10 keywords after the abstract.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Context, state of the art, and aim.

sections.heading: Materials and Methods
sections.guidance: Reproducible detail; MDPI encourages subsections.

sections.heading: Results
sections.guidance: Findings; may be combined with Discussion.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Interpretation in context; limitations.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.guidance: Main conclusions and future directions.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: MDPI numbered style. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Decimal numbered sections + line numbers reflect MDPI's review template; A4 per MDPI. Spacing/font/margins are Gaply defaults. MDPI's camera-ready (Palatino template) is typeset by MDPI — not reproduced.

latexFormat.source: MDPI publishes single-column A4 with numbered sections. Gaply's reading layout, not the MDPI class.

scaffolds.label: Taylor & Francis-style (unofficial)
scaffolds.noticeText: Taylor & Francis-style is Gaply's own scaffold informed by T&F's public author guidance — not an official T&F template. T&F journals use several standard reference styles (default here: T&F Chicago author-date); verify your target journal at the T&F author services page.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.guidance: Single paragraph; check the journal for a word limit (often ~200).

sections.heading: Keywords
sections.guidance: Indexing terms as required by the journal.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.guidance: Context, gap, and aim.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.guidance: Design and procedures.

sections.heading: Results
sections.guidance: Findings.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.guidance: Interpretation and implications.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.guidance: Summary and future work.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: Journal-specific T&F standard style. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Many Taylor & Francis journals request double-spaced, line-numbered manuscripts for review. Section numbering, font, margins, and page size are Gaply defaults; exact rules are journal-specific — verify at the link.

latexFormat.source: Varies widely across T&F journals; single-column A4 is the safe reading default. Not the interact class.

sections.heading: References
sections.guidance: Journal-specific Wiley style. Gaply formats these (Set B).

docxFormat.source: Many Wiley journals request double-spaced, line-numbered manuscripts for review. Section numbering, font, margins, and page size are Gaply defaults; Wiley has no single house format — verify at the link.

latexFormat.source: Two-column A4 is the common Wiley published look. Gaply's reading layout, not a Wiley class.
